# [Feat] [Intel] lora: Add intel_xpu LoRA backend

## Motivation

On Intel XPU, multi-LoRA serving currently has to use the generic `triton`, `csgmv`, or `torch_native` backends. This PR adds an `intel_xpu` LoRA backend that runs the native Intel XPU LoRA kernels from [sgl-kernel-xpu](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu) on both the prefill and decode paths.

Usage:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <base-model> \
    --device xpu \
    --enable-lora \
    --lora-paths <name>=<adapter-path> \
    --lora-backend intel_xpu
```

## Dependency: sgl-kernel-xpu

The backend imports these ops from `sgl_kernel` (sgl-kernel-xpu):

| Op | Used for | PR (merged and closed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding_lora_a_fwd` | Embedding LoRA A | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/207) |
| `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/262) |
| `sgemm_lora_b_fwd` | LoRA B expand, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/356) |
| `qkv_lora_b_fwd` | Fused QKV LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/393) |
| `gate_up_lora_b_fwd` | Fused gate/up LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/490) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, decode | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/506) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd` | LoRA B expand, decode (single, QKV, and gate/up slices) | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/523) |

These kernels especially decode kernels are optimized. To get the best performance, build sgl-kernel-xpu from the PR below:

- [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/550) - <Decode LoRA kernels are optimized>

This PR should merge after the above PR got merged in sgl-kernel-xpu.

## Modifications

**New backend**: `python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/intel_xpu_backend.py` (`IntelXpuLoRABackend`)
- Prefill (contiguous batch metadata, `permutation is None`): per-shape XPU kernels (`sgemm_lora_a_fwd`, `sgemm_lora_b_fwd`, `qkv_lora_b_fwd`, `gate_up_lora_b_fwd`).
- Decode: tokens are sorted by adapter (`compute_sgemm_routing`), and the chunked-SGMV shrink/expand pair are gather fused DPAS kernels. The shrink output layout `(num_tokens, num_slices * max_rank)` is exactly the expand's input, so decode stays on XPU from A to B. The expand fuses per-adapter scaling and the `base_output` residual.
- Supports decode and prefill graph capture (`supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True`, 32 fixed prefill segment slots). Batches with more requests fall back to eager prefill.
- Batch preparation (segment routing, lm_head pruning, graph metadata) follows the triton backend's `LoRABatchInfo` layout.

**Registration and CLI**
- `lora/backend/lora_registry.py`: register `intel_xpu`.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`: add `LORA_BACKEND_CHOICES` (including `intel_xpu`). `arg_groups/fields/lora.py` now reads `--lora-backend` choices from it instead of a hardcoded list, and `server_args.py` re-exports it with the other choice lists.

**Validation**
- `arg_groups/validation_hook.py`: `validate_device_lora_backend` rejects `--lora-backend intel_xpu` without `--device xpu` at argument-check time. Without it, the error only appears later as an import failure inside `LoRAManager` init. This mirrors the existing `--sampling-backend intel_xpu` check.

**Tests**
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: `TestIntelXpuLoRABackend` (CPU CI) checks that the backend is registered and selectable from the CLI, rejected off XPU, and accepted on XPU.
- `test/manual/lora/test_lora_xpu_basics.py`: add `intel_xpu` to `DENSE_BACKENDS`, so it runs the HF+PEFT logprob comparison and the multi-LoRA batching / drainer routing tests next to `triton`, `csgmv`, and `torch_native`.

## Accuracy Tests

Models and adapters are the ones defined for `test/manual/lora/test_lora_backend.py`. Each case runs 4 engines (SRT+LoRA, SRT base, HF+LoRA, HF base) with `--lora-backend intel_xpu` and compares top input/output logprobs against HF plus ROUGE-L of the decoded text. fp16, `max_new_tokens=32`, 2 prompts per case (values are prompt 0 / prompt 1); limits: logprob diff `< 1e-1`, ROUGE-L `1.0`.

| Base model | Adapter | Max prefill logprob diff | Max decode logprob diff | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | nvidia/llama-3.1-nemoguard-8b-topic-control | 0.0155 / 0.0339 | 0.0310 / 0.0234 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-2-7b-hf | winddude/wizardLM-LlaMA-LoRA-7B | 0.0161 / 0.0312 | 0.0310 / 0.0312 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | algoprog/fact-generation-llama-3.1-8b-instruct-lora | 0.0177 / 0.0312 | 0.0312 / 0.0301 | 1.0 / 1.0 | 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct

**Setup**
- Model: `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `--tp-size 8` on 8 Intel XPU cards, `--dtype bfloat16`, `--attention-backend triton`, `--disable-radix-cache`, graph capture on.
- LoRA: 4 bf16 adapters (`adamkarvonen/llama3.3_70b_shuffled_e3_v2`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_sft`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_speed60_bos`, `vineetdaniels/llama33_70b_icd_cpt`), `--max-loras-per-batch 4`, adapters drawn uniformly per request. `base` is the same model served with LoRA disabled.
- Client: SGLang serving benchmark, random dataset with lengths pinned (`--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `ignore_eos` on, so every request emits exactly `output_len` tokens), request rate inf, fixed concurrency. Every run completed all requests with exactly `num_requests * output_len` generated tokens.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (no LoRA) | 1547.27 | 2014.09 | 2290.23 | 2681.61 |
| `csgmv` | 1145.49 | 2849.50 | 3163.06 | 3618.87 |
| `triton` | 1121.21 | 2915.09 | 3210.81 | 3694.60 |
| `intel_xpu`* | **1295.14** | **2337.53** | **2881.13** | **3203.76** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +13.1%, mean TTFT -18.0%.

In `decode_128_4lora`, mean TTFT is higher with `intel_xpu` than with `csgmv` (2299 vs 1579 ms, +46 %). Each request has a 16-token prompt, so TTFT there is mostly time spent queueing for a slot in the full decode batch rather than prefill compute (base TTFT also grows with concurrency), and it is 23 % of `intel_xpu`'s end-to-end latency. Mean E2E latency is still 15 % lower than `csgmv`'s (10140 vs 11895 ms); total throughput, TPOT, and E2E latency are the meaningful metrics for decode scenarios.

The base (no-LoRA) path is unchanged by this PR: it only adds the `intel_xpu` LoRA backend, its `--lora-backend` choice, and the `--device xpu` check.

detail.body:
# [Feat] [Intel] lora: Add intel_xpu LoRA backend

## Motivation

On Intel XPU, multi-LoRA serving currently has to use the generic `triton`, `csgmv`, or `torch_native` backends. This PR adds an `intel_xpu` LoRA backend that runs the native Intel XPU LoRA kernels from [sgl-kernel-xpu](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu) on both the prefill and decode paths.

Usage:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <base-model> \
    --device xpu \
    --enable-lora \
    --lora-paths <name>=<adapter-path> \
    --lora-backend intel_xpu
```

## Dependency: sgl-kernel-xpu

The backend imports these ops from `sgl_kernel` (sgl-kernel-xpu):

| Op | Used for | PR (merged and closed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding_lora_a_fwd` | Embedding LoRA A | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/207) |
| `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/262) |
| `sgemm_lora_b_fwd` | LoRA B expand, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/356) |
| `qkv_lora_b_fwd` | Fused QKV LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/393) |
| `gate_up_lora_b_fwd` | Fused gate/up LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/490) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, decode | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/506) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd` | LoRA B expand, decode (single, QKV, and gate/up slices) | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/523) |

These kernels especially decode kernels are optimized. To get the best performance, build sgl-kernel-xpu from the PR below:

- [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/550) - <Decode LoRA kernels are optimized>

This PR should merge after the above PR got merged in sgl-kernel-xpu.

## Modifications

**New backend**: `python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/intel_xpu_backend.py` (`IntelXpuLoRABackend`)
- Prefill (contiguous batch metadata, `permutation is None`): per-shape XPU kernels (`sgemm_lora_a_fwd`, `sgemm_lora_b_fwd`, `qkv_lora_b_fwd`, `gate_up_lora_b_fwd`).
- Decode: tokens are sorted by adapter (`compute_sgemm_routing`), and the chunked-SGMV shrink/expand pair are gather fused DPAS kernels. The shrink output layout `(num_tokens, num_slices * max_rank)` is exactly the expand's input, so decode stays on XPU from A to B. The expand fuses per-adapter scaling and the `base_output` residual.
- Supports decode and prefill graph capture (`supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True`, 32 fixed prefill segment slots). Batches with more requests fall back to eager prefill.
- Batch preparation (segment routing, lm_head pruning, graph metadata) follows the triton backend's `LoRABatchInfo` layout.

**Registration and CLI**
- `lora/backend/lora_registry.py`: register `intel_xpu`.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`: add `LORA_BACKEND_CHOICES` (including `intel_xpu`). `arg_groups/fields/lora.py` now reads `--lora-backend` choices from it instead of a hardcoded list, and `server_args.py` re-exports it with the other choice lists.

**Validation**
- `arg_groups/validation_hook.py`: `validate_device_lora_backend` rejects `--lora-backend intel_xpu` without `--device xpu` at argument-check time. Without it, the error only appears later as an import failure inside `LoRAManager` init. This mirrors the existing `--sampling-backend intel_xpu` check.

**Tests**
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: `TestIntelXpuLoRABackend` (CPU CI) checks that the backend is registered and selectable from the CLI, rejected off XPU, and accepted on XPU.
- `test/manual/lora/test_lora_xpu_basics.py`: add `intel_xpu` to `DENSE_BACKENDS`, so it runs the HF+PEFT logprob comparison and the multi-LoRA batching / drainer routing tests next to `triton`, `csgmv`, and `torch_native`.

## Accuracy Tests

Models and adapters are the ones defined for `test/manual/lora/test_lora_backend.py`. Each case runs 4 engines (SRT+LoRA, SRT base, HF+LoRA, HF base) with `--lora-backend intel_xpu` and compares top input/output logprobs against HF plus ROUGE-L of the decoded text. fp16, `max_new_tokens=32`, 2 prompts per case (values are prompt 0 / prompt 1); limits: logprob diff `< 1e-1`, ROUGE-L `1.0`.

+import dataclasses
+from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+# Native Intel XPU LoRA kernels (from sgl-kernel-xpu). Aliased with an `xpu_`
+# prefix to keep the kernel family explicit at each call site.
+from sgl_kernel import (
+    chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd as xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_forward,
+)
+from sgl_kernel import (
+    chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd as xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_forward,
+)
+from sgl_kernel import embedding_lora_a_fwd as xpu_embedding_lora_a_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import gate_up_lora_b_fwd as xpu_gate_up_lora_b_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import qkv_lora_b_fwd as xpu_qkv_lora_b_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import sgemm_lora_a_fwd as xpu_sgemm_lora_a_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import sgemm_lora_b_fwd as xpu_sgemm_lora_b_fwd
+
+from sglang.srt.lora.backend.base_backend import BaseLoRABackend
+from sglang.srt.lora.utils import (
+    LoRABatchInfo,
+    get_lm_head_pruned_lens,
+    merge_and_chunk_segments,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardBatch
+
+# Fixed segment slots (one per request) baked into the captured prefill LoRA
+# kernel grids; batches with more requests fall back to eager prefill.
+PREFILL_CUDA_GRAPH_LORA_SEGMENTS = 32
+
+
+class IntelXpuLoRABackend(BaseLoRABackend):
+    """LoRA on native Intel XPU kernels: per-shape sgemm kernels for contiguous prefill,
+    chunked-SGMV (gather/GEMM/scatter by permutation) for adapter-sorted decode."""
+
+    name = "intel_xpu"
+    supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        max_loras_per_batch: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(max_loras_per_batch, device)
+        # Merged-segment variant of batch_info; set alongside it in
+        # prepare_lora_batch and cleared together in reset_batch_state.
+        self.sgemm_batch_info: Optional[LoRABatchInfo] = None
+        self.cuda_graph_sgemm_batch_info: Optional[LoRABatchInfo] = None
+
+    def reset_batch_state(self):
+        super().reset_batch_state()
+        self.sgemm_batch_info = None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _is_permuted(batch_info: LoRABatchInfo) -> bool:
+        """True when the batch metadata is adapter-sorted (decode), in which
+        case the contiguous-only XPU kernels cannot be used."""
+        return batch_info.permutation is not None
+
+    def _sgemm_info(self, pruned_batch_info=None):
+        """Return the sgemm batch_info (merged segments when available)."""
+        if pruned_batch_info is not None:
+            return pruned_batch_info
+        assert self.batch_info is not None, (
+            "LoRA kernel invoked with no prepared batch (DP-attention idle "
+            "forward?). Gate the caller on lora_active, as in "
+            "sglang/srt/lora/layers.py forwards."
+        )
+        return self.sgemm_batch_info or self.batch_info
+
+    def _lora_a_shrink(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        sgemm_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+        stack_num: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """LoRA A shrink: sgemm_lora_a_fwd on prefill, chunked-SGMV on decode (no
+        max_chunk_size needed). Output is always in physical token order."""
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            return xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_forward(
+                input_x=x,
+                weights=weights,
+                stack_num=stack_num,
+                num_segments=sgemm_info.num_segments,
+                seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+                weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+                lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+                permutation=sgemm_info.permutation,
+            )
+        return xpu_sgemm_lora_a_fwd(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            stack_num=stack_num,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+        )
+
+    def _lora_b_expand(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        sgemm_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+        slice_offsets: torch.Tensor,
+        max_slice_size: int,
+        num_slices: int,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Decode-only chunked-SGMV B expand; takes the shrink's (num_tokens,
+        num_slices * max_rank) output as-is and fuses scaling and base_output."""
+        return xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_forward(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            slice_offsets=slice_offsets,
+            max_slice_size=max_slice_size,
+            num_slices=num_slices,
+            num_segments=sgemm_info.num_segments,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            permutation=sgemm_info.permutation,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    # ---- LoRA kernel entry points ----
+
+    def run_lora_a_embedding(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        vocab_size: int,
+        extra_embeddings: torch.Tensor = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # self.batch_info is always contiguous (permutation=None) for
+        # embeddings, so the XPU kernel always applies.
+        bi = self.batch_info
+        assert bi is not None, (
+            "LoRA kernel invoked with no prepared batch (DP-attention idle "
+            "forward?). Gate the caller on lora_active."
+        )
+        return xpu_embedding_lora_a_fwd(
+            input_ids=input_ids,
+            weights=weights,
+            vocab_size=vocab_size,
+            max_len=bi.max_len,
+            seg_indptr=bi.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=bi.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=bi.lora_ranks,
+            extra_embeddings=extra_embeddings,
+            seg_lens=bi.seg_lens,
+        )
+
+    def run_lora_a_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        stack_num: int = 1,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        return self._lora_a_shrink(x, weights, sgemm_info, stack_num)
+
+    def run_lora_b_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): single-slice chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=x,
+                weights=weights,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=weights.shape[-2],
+                num_slices=1,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+        return xpu_sgemm_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def run_qkv_lora(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        qkv_lora_a: torch.Tensor,
+        qkv_lora_b: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        max_qkv_out_dim: int,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        n_slices: int = 3,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+        # x: (s, input_dim), qkv_lora_a: (num_lora, n_slices * r, input_dim),
+        # qkv_lora_b: (num_lora, total_output_dim, r)
+        assert isinstance(qkv_lora_b, torch.Tensor)
+
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info()
+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted
+        # decode); its output is in physical token order.
+        lora_a_output = self._lora_a_shrink(x, qkv_lora_a, sgemm_info, n_slices)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): fused n_slices-way chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=lora_a_output,
+                weights=qkv_lora_b,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=max_qkv_out_dim,
+                num_slices=n_slices,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+
+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_qkv_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            qkv_lora_b=qkv_lora_b,
+            output_offset=output_offset,
+            max_qkv_out_dim=max_qkv_out_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def run_gate_up_lora(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        gate_up_lora_a: torch.Tensor,
+        gate_up_lora_b: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+        # x: (s, input_dim), gate_up_lora_a: (num_lora, 2 * r, input_dim),
+        # gate_up_lora_b: (num_lora, 2 * output_dim, r)
+        assert isinstance(gate_up_lora_b, torch.Tensor)
+        output_dim = gate_up_lora_b.shape[-2] // 2
+
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info()
+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted
+        # decode); its output is in physical token order.
+        lora_a_output = self._lora_a_shrink(x, gate_up_lora_a, sgemm_info, 2)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): fused 2-way (gate, up) chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=lora_a_output,
+                weights=gate_up_lora_b,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=output_dim,
+                num_slices=2,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+
+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_gate_up_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            gate_up_lora_b=gate_up_lora_b,
+            output_dim=output_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    # ---- Batch preparation (mirrors the triton backend's LoRABatchInfo layout) ----
+
+    def init_cuda_graph_batch_info(
+        self,
+        max_bs_in_cuda_graph: int,
+        num_tokens_per_req: int,
+    ):
+        max_tokens = max_bs_in_cuda_graph * num_tokens_per_req
+        mlpb = self.max_loras_per_batch
+        with torch.device(self.device):
+            self.cuda_graph_batch_info = LoRABatchInfo(
+                bs=max_bs_in_cuda_graph,
+                use_cuda_graph=True,
+                num_segments=None,
+                seg_lens=torch.full(
+                    (max_bs_in_cuda_graph,), num_tokens_per_req, dtype=torch.int32
+                ),
+                seg_indptr=torch.zeros(max_bs_in_cuda_graph + 1, dtype=torch.int32),
+                max_len=num_tokens_per_req,
+                weight_indices=torch.zeros(max_bs_in_cuda_graph, dtype=torch.int32),
+                lora_ranks=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                scalings=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.float),
+                permutation=None,
+            )
+
+            torch.cumsum(
+                self.cuda_graph_batch_info.seg_lens[:max_bs_in_cuda_graph],
+                dim=0,
+                out=self.cuda_graph_batch_info.seg_indptr[1 : max_bs_in_cuda_graph + 1],
+            )
+
+            # Sgemm batch_info with segments merged by adapter.
+            # Updated each batch by compute_sgemm_routing().
+            self.cuda_graph_sgemm_batch_info = LoRABatchInfo(
+                bs=mlpb,
+                use_cuda_graph=True,
+                num_segments=mlpb,
+                seg_lens=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                seg_indptr=torch.zeros(mlpb + 1, dtype=torch.int32),
+                max_len=max_tokens,
+                weight_indices=torch.arange(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                lora_ranks=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                scalings=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.float),
+                permutation=torch.zeros(max_tokens, dtype=torch.int32),
+            )
+
+    def init_prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info(self, max_num_tokens: int):
+        num_slots = PREFILL_CUDA_GRAPH_LORA_SEGMENTS
+        mlpb = self.max_loras_per_batch

+            # bs pinned at num_slots so the captured grids cover any replay
+            # batch; slots past the live batch keep seg_lens == 0 and no-op.
+            self.prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info = LoRABatchInfo(
+                bs=num_slots,
+                use_cuda_graph=True,
+                num_segments=num_slots,
+                seg_lens=torch.zeros(num_slots, dtype=torch.int32),
+                seg_indptr=torch.zeros(num_slots + 1, dtype=torch.int32),
+                max_len=0,
+                weight_indices=torch.zeros(num_slots, dtype=torch.int32),
+                lora_ranks=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                scalings=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.float),
+                permutation=None,
+            )
+        self.prefill_cuda_graph_max_bs = num_slots
+        self.prefill_cuda_graph_max_tokens = max_num_tokens
+
+    def compute_sgemm_routing(self, use_cuda_graph: bool):
+        """Sort tokens by adapter and build merged segments for sgemm LoRA."""
+        bi = self.batch_info
+        bs = bi.bs
+        mlpb = self.max_loras_per_batch
+        wi = bi.weight_indices[:bs]
+
+        perm = torch.argsort(wi, stable=True).to(torch.int32)
+        sorted_wi = wi[perm]
+        adapter_ids = torch.arange(mlpb, device=wi.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        seg_starts = torch.searchsorted(sorted_wi, adapter_ids)
+        seg_ends = torch.searchsorted(sorted_wi, adapter_ids, right=True)
+        seg_lens = seg_ends - seg_starts
+
+        if use_cuda_graph:
+            sgemm = self.cuda_graph_sgemm_batch_info

+            sgemm.seg_lens[:] = seg_lens
+            sgemm.seg_indptr[0:1].zero_()

+            sgemm.scalings[:mlpb] = bi.scalings[:mlpb]

+            seg_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(seg_lens, dim=0)
+            sgemm = LoRABatchInfo(
+                bs=mlpb,
+                use_cuda_graph=False,
+                num_segments=mlpb,
+                seg_lens=seg_lens,
+                seg_indptr=seg_indptr,
+                max_len=bs,
+                weight_indices=adapter_ids,
+                lora_ranks=bi.lora_ranks[:mlpb].clone(),
+                scalings=bi.scalings[:mlpb].clone(),
+                permutation=perm,
+            )

+        self.sgemm_batch_info = sgemm
+
+    def prepare_lora_batch(
+        self,
+        forward_batch: ForwardBatch,
+        weight_indices: list[int],
+        lora_ranks: list[int],
+        scalings: list[float],
+        use_cuda_graph: bool,
+        use_prefill_cuda_graph: bool = False,
+    ):
+        # Use pinned memory to avoid synchronizations during host-to-device transfer
+        weight_indices_tensor = torch.tensor(
+            weight_indices, dtype=torch.int32, pin_memory=True, device="cpu"
+        )
+        lora_ranks_tensor = torch.tensor(
+            lora_ranks, dtype=torch.int32, pin_memory=True, device="cpu"
+        )
+        scalings_tensor = torch.tensor(
+            scalings, dtype=torch.float, pin_memory=True, device="cpu"
+        )

+        bs = forward_batch.batch_size
+
+        if use_cuda_graph:
+            assert self.cuda_graph_batch_info is not None, (
+                "CUDA Graph batch info is not initialized."
+            )
+            batch_info = self.cuda_graph_batch_info
+            batch_info.bs = forward_batch.batch_size
+            batch_info.num_segments = forward_batch.batch_size
+        elif use_prefill_cuda_graph:
+            batch_info = self.prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info
+            # bs stays pinned at the allocated slot count; slots past the
+            # live batch no-op via seg_lens == 0.
+            batch_info.num_segments = bs
+            batch_info.max_len = max(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu)
+            batch_info.seg_lens[:bs].copy_(
+                forward_batch.extend_seq_lens, non_blocking=True
+            )
+            batch_info.seg_lens[bs:].zero_()

+        else:
+            max_len = (
+                # Calculate max_len from the CPU copy to avoid D2H transfer.
+                max(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu)
+                if forward_batch.forward_mode.is_extend()
+                else 1
+            )
+            seg_lens = (
+                forward_batch.extend_seq_lens
+                if forward_batch.forward_mode.is_extend()
+                else torch.ones(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+            )
+            seg_indptr = torch.zeros((bs + 1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+            seg_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(seg_lens, dim=0)
+
+            batch_info = LoRABatchInfo(
+                bs=forward_batch.batch_size,
+                num_segments=forward_batch.batch_size,
+                max_len=max_len,
+                use_cuda_graph=False,
+                seg_lens=seg_lens,
+                seg_indptr=seg_indptr,
+                weight_indices=torch.empty(
+                    (bs,), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+                ),
+                lora_ranks=torch.empty(
+                    # int32: the XPU LoRA kernels require int32 lora_ranks (the
+                    # CUDA-graph paths above already allocate int32).
+                    (self.max_loras_per_batch,),
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device=self.device,
+                ),
+                scalings=torch.empty(
+                    (self.max_loras_per_batch,), dtype=torch.float, device=self.device
+                ),
+                permutation=None,
+            )
+
+        # Copy to device asynchronously
+        batch_info.lora_ranks[: self.max_loras_per_batch].copy_(
+            lora_ranks_tensor, non_blocking=True
+        )
+        batch_info.scalings[: self.max_loras_per_batch].copy_(
+            scalings_tensor, non_blocking=True
+        )
+        batch_info.weight_indices[:bs].copy_(weight_indices_tensor, non_blocking=True)
+
+        batch_info = self._add_moe_lora_info(forward_batch, batch_info)
+        self.batch_info = batch_info
+
+        # Biggest win is in decode.
+        is_decode = not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_extend()
+        if is_decode:
+            self.compute_sgemm_routing(use_cuda_graph)
+        else:
+            self.sgemm_batch_info = None
+
+        self.lm_head_batch_info, self.lm_head_pass_batch_infos = (
+            self._prepare_lm_head_batch_info(forward_batch, weight_indices, batch_info)
+        )
+
+    def _prepare_lm_head_batch_info(
+        self,
+        forward_batch: ForwardBatch,
+        weight_indices: list[int],
+        batch_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+    ) -> Tuple[Optional[LoRABatchInfo], Optional[List[LoRABatchInfo]]]:
+
+        # Precompute lm_head_batch_info for pruned lm_head LoRA
+        pruned_lens = get_lm_head_pruned_lens(forward_batch)
+        lm_head_batch_info = None
+        lm_head_pass_batch_infos = None
+
+        if pruned_lens is not None:
+            pruned_total = sum(pruned_lens)
+            lm_head_segments = merge_and_chunk_segments(
+                weight_indices, pruned_lens, chunk_size=pruned_total
+            )
+            lm_head_batch_info = self._build_lm_head_batch_info(
+                lm_head_segments, batch_info, pruned_total
+            )
+
+            # Precompute per-pass batch_infos for logprobs chunking
+            pass_segments = self._get_lm_head_pass_segments(weight_indices, pruned_lens)
+            if pass_segments is not None:
+                lm_head_pass_batch_infos = []
+                for seg_wi, seg_lens_list in pass_segments:
+                    pass_total = sum(seg_lens_list)
+                    merged_segments = merge_and_chunk_segments(
+                        seg_wi, seg_lens_list, chunk_size=pass_total
+                    )
+                    lm_head_pass_batch_infos.append(
+                        self._build_lm_head_batch_info(
+                            merged_segments, batch_info, pass_total
+                        )
+                    )
+
+        return lm_head_batch_info, lm_head_pass_batch_infos
+
+    def _build_lm_head_batch_info(
+        self,
+        lm_head_segments: Tuple[List[int], List[int]],
+        batch_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+        expected_tokens: int,
+    ) -> LoRABatchInfo:
+        seg_weight_indices_cpu, seg_lens_cpu = lm_head_segments
+        num_segments = len(seg_weight_indices_cpu)
+
+        seg_lens = torch.tensor(seg_lens_cpu, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+        seg_indptr = torch.zeros(
+            (num_segments + 1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+        )
+        seg_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(seg_lens, dim=0)
+
+        return dataclasses.replace(
+            batch_info,
+            # lm_head LoRA runs in the eager tail outside any captured prefill
+            # graph, on freshly allocated pruned metadata.
+            use_cuda_graph=False,
+            bs=num_segments,
+            num_segments=num_segments,
+            max_len=max(seg_lens_cpu),
+            seg_lens=seg_lens,
+            seg_indptr=seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=torch.tensor(
+                seg_weight_indices_cpu, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+            ),
+            expected_tokens=expected_tokens,
+        )

+            vocab_size=vocab_size,
+            max_len=bi.max_len,
+            seg_indptr=bi.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=bi.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=bi.lora_ranks,
+            extra_embeddings=extra_embeddings,
+            seg_lens=bi.seg_lens,
+        )
+
+    def run_lora_a_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        stack_num: int = 1,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        return self._lora_a_shrink(x, weights, sgemm_info, stack_num)
+
+    def run_lora_b_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): single-slice chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=x,
+                weights=weights,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=weights.shape[-2],
+                num_slices=1,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+        return xpu_sgemm_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def run_qkv_lora(

+        qkv_lora_a: torch.Tensor,

+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        n_slices: int = 3,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+        # x: (s, input_dim), qkv_lora_a: (num_lora, n_slices * r, input_dim),
+        # qkv_lora_b: (num_lora, total_output_dim, r)
+        assert isinstance(qkv_lora_b, torch.Tensor)
+
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info()
+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted
+        # decode); its output is in physical token order.
+        lora_a_output = self._lora_a_shrink(x, qkv_lora_a, sgemm_info, n_slices)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): fused n_slices-way chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=lora_a_output,
+                weights=qkv_lora_b,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=max_qkv_out_dim,
+                num_slices=n_slices,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+
+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_qkv_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            qkv_lora_b=qkv_lora_b,
+            output_offset=output_offset,
+            max_qkv_out_dim=max_qkv_out_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,

+    def run_gate_up_lora(

+        x: torch.Tensor,

+        gate_up_lora_b: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+

+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted

+            )

+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_gate_up_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            gate_up_lora_b=gate_up_lora_b,
+            output_dim=output_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,

+                permutation=torch.zeros(max_tokens, dtype=torch.int32),

+    def init_prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info(self, max_num_tokens: int):
+        num_slots = PREFILL_CUDA_GRAPH_LORA_SEGMENTS

+        with torch.device(self.device):
+            # bs pinned at num_slots so the captured grids cover any replay

+            self.prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info = LoRABatchInfo(

+                use_cuda_graph=True,
+                num_segments=num_slots,
+                seg_lens=torch.zeros(num_slots, dtype=torch.int32),
+                seg_indptr=torch.zeros(num_slots + 1, dtype=torch.int32),

+                weight_indices=torch.zeros(num_slots, dtype=torch.int32),
+                lora_ranks=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.int32),
+                scalings=torch.zeros(mlpb, dtype=torch.float),
+                permutation=None,
+            )
+        self.prefill_cuda_graph_max_bs = num_slots
+        self.prefill_cuda_graph_max_tokens = max_num_tokens
+
+    def compute_sgemm_routing(self, use_cuda_graph: bool):
+        """Sort tokens by adapter and build merged segments for sgemm LoRA."""
+        bi = self.batch_info
+        bs = bi.bs
+        mlpb = self.max_loras_per_batch

+        perm = torch.argsort(wi, stable=True).to(torch.int32)

+        seg_starts = torch.searchsorted(sorted_wi, adapter_ids)
